claims.text: An approximately 50 nm conformal Al2O3 coating can be deposited on zirconium-alloy cladding by atomic layer deposition.
ALD deposition will produce a continuous, defect-free, nanostructured alumina layer.
The alumina layer will adhere strongly to the zirconium-alloy substrate.
Dense Al2O3 acts as an oxygen-diffusion barrier at high temperature.
The alumina coating impedes oxygen transport to the zirconium alloy.
Impeding oxygen transport reduces rapid oxidation of the zirconium alloy.
Reduced zirconium-oxide formation helps preserve cladding integrity.
ALD-coated cladding will have a significantly lower oxidation rate than uncoated cladding during high-temperature steam exposure.
ALD-coated cladding will have lower weight gain than uncoated cladding during high-temperature steam exposure.
The coated cladding will retain mechanical stability suitable for service.
The coated cladding will retain irradiation stability suitable for service.
The expected oxidation benefit applies in steam at approximately 900–1200 °C under irradiation and mechanical loading conditions.
The oxidation benefit depends on the alumina coating remaining intact and adherent during prolonged high-temperature and irradiation exposure.
Coating degradation, spallation, or other loss of integrity may eliminate the oxidation benefit.
Thermal-expansion mismatch during transients may threaten coating compatibility or adherence.
A failure to achieve at least a 20% reduction in oxidation rate or weight gain relative to an uncoated control would falsify the hypothesis.
Degradation or spallation of the alumina coating during testing would falsify the hypothesis.
